answer.rationale: With only 14 days until contract expiration and the line running at 94% of committed volume with no buffer, switching primary vendors now carries real delivery risk despite meeting the cost mandate outright (memory_c2 describes a prior successful switch but doesn't establish that onboarding speed generalizes to a zero-buffer, time-constrained scenario). Renewing incumbent alone doesn't address the 18% mandate. Negotiating terms with the incumbent, using market benchmarking (memory_c4) and precedent for multi-year volume pricing (memory_c6), can recover meaningful cost without introducing migration or qualification risk, while preserving the stability track record (memory_c1). This doesn't fully guarantee the 18% target is met, so I'm flagging that downstream cost risk explicitly rather than assuming negotiation will close the full gap — if it falls short, switching or second-sourcing remains available next cycle. Verifying memory_c4's archived record before committing since it's the load-bearing claim for this action's expected savings magnitude.
